Thanks Jonas — helpful recap.

A few clarifying items before Marissa weighs in:

- Subprocessors: Do you provide a current list and commit to 30 days' notice for additions? Our procurement prefers explicit approval for new subprocessors.
- Breach notice: We need 72-hour notification for any confirmed data breach affecting PII. Is that acceptable?
- Data residency: We will need EU-only processing for EU customer data; can Redwood commit to EU-only hosting for those buckets and provide proof (region/cluster IDs)?
- Retention & deletion: What's the default retention period for logs and model inputs? We need a retention policy and deletion process within 30 days after contract termination.
- Logging controls: Can you confirm what fields are redacted from logs and if access is role-based with audit logs?

If Marissa could annotate the DPA and point to where these are addressed, that would be ideal.

Hi Samantha / Raj — thanks for the clear list. I've gone through the DPA and annotated relevant sections (attached: DPA_annotated_acme_v1.pdf). Below are the concise answers to each of your points; happy to expand or hop on a follow-up call with security/legal.

1) Controller / Processor
- Per section 1.1 of the DPA: Acme Payments is the Controller and Redwood Inference is the Processor for customer-provided data processed via the Redwood platform (hosted/dedicated/private deployments as specified). For any features where customer-initiated hosting or bring-your-own-model changes control boundaries, we call that out in the SOW.

2) Subprocessors
- We maintain a current list of subprocessors here: https://redwood-inference.com/subprocessors/acme_current_list.csv.
- Standard notice: we provide 30 days' notice for planned additions and a right to object where a downstream subprocessor introduces material risk. In emergency situations (e.g., urgent failover to maintain availability), we will notify you as soon as practicable and provide remediation details.

3) Breach Notice
- Redwood commits to notifying Customer of any confirmed breach affecting Customer PII within 72 hours of confirmation. We also provide an initial alert within 24 hours if we are still investigating and have actionable preliminary information.

4) Data Residency
- We support regional tenancy and can pin customer data to EU-only processing for EU customer data when you select our EU deployment option (Dedicated or Private). For hosted customers, we have an EU region (e.g., eu-west-1 clusters ID: eu-cluster-42) and can include region/cluster identifiers in the SOW/attestation.

5) Retention & Deletion
- Default telemetry/log retention: 90 days for non-production diagnostic logs; model inputs are not retained by default for training purposes.
- Opt-in retention: Customers can enable longer retention windows for debugging/metrics; this must be explicitly enabled.
- Contract termination: we commit to deleting Customer data and model inputs within 30 days of contract termination for hosted/dedicated deployments unless a different timeline is agreed in the SOW. We'll provide deletion confirmation and export copies as requested.

6) Logging & PII Controls
- By default, Redwood does not persist raw PII fields. Our platform provides configurable redaction rules; we can redact email addresses, SSNs, and other sensitive fields before logs are stored.
- Access control: role-based access with audited access logs (who/when/why). We retain access audit logs for 12 months by default; access to raw request payloads is restricted to a small group (SRE/security) and requires justification.

Attachments / Links:
- Attached: DPA_annotated_acme_v1.pdf with inline references to sections above.
- Subprocessors list: https://redwood-inference.com/subprocessors/acme_current_list.csv
- SOC 2 / security package: we can share our security questionnaire and SOC 2 report via secure link on request.

If these terms look good, we can provision the EU-only tenancy for your pilot and include the region IDs in the SOW. Jonas — happy if you schedule a short follow-up with Samantha & Raj for any final procurement items.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
